title: Errands
dek: Every letter this archive has written, in full - drafted, sent and answered - so that a draft is a page somebody can act from and not a file nobody opens.
lead: A reading that cannot be done from the films ends at a person: a parish priest, an archivist, a custodian. These are the letters to them. Each says who is being asked, what for, and what the answer would settle, and carries the text. Nothing on this page has been sent by the site; sending is a person's decision, and the state shown is the state of the letter.

draft: written and kept here; nothing has gone out
sent: sent; no answer yet, or only an acknowledgement
answered: sent and answered - kept because the answer is the finding

tallyNote: A negative or a refused request is kept as a result, here and on [the search register](/searched/).
close: Where a letter has been answered, the answer is on the work list and the search register. A draft's address is marked to be confirmed where this archive has not verified it; nothing here invents a street or an inbox.

Poštovani gospodine župniče,

obraćam Vam se s molbom za pomoć u istraživanju obiteljske povijesti. Tražim dva

I am researching the family of my grandmother, HEDVIGA "SEKA" BLAŽEVIĆ, born at
Senj in 1926. Her father's mother was TEREZA ŽUBRINIĆ, born at Otočac on
29 November 1867. The work is published, free and without advertising, at:

https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

Anything you send would be published there in full and credited. A negative
answer is worth having too, and I publish those as results.

WHAT I HAVE ALREADY READ. Tereza's parents were NIKOLA (Nicolaus) ŽUBRINIĆ,
born at Otočac on 24 January 1834, and ANA, his wife. In your baptismal
register, read from the filmed copy, they are at ŠUMEĆICA No. 2:

3 July 1856 Stjepan — mother entered "Anna nata Štrumbulko"
15 September 1858 Marija — mother entered "Anna Marić"

The same woman is written with two different family names two years apart. I
think the first is a house name (a nadimak) and the second her surname, but that
is an inference from two entries, not something any document says.

===========================================================================
1. Ana's own baptism — the one thing that would name her parents
===========================================================================

Ana had a first child in 1853, so she was born between about 1830 and 1836. The
filmed copy of your baptismal register begins in SEPTEMBER 1834, so a baptism
before that month is on no film I can reach, and I have looked at the first
months after it without finding her.

1a. The baptism of ANA MARIĆ ("Štrumbulko"), Otočac, about 1830-1836. It
would give her father's given name, her mother's name, and the house.

===========================================================================
2. Their marriage
===========================================================================

2a. The marriage of NIKOLA ŽUBRINIĆ and ANA MARIĆ, about 1850-1852. I cannot
find it in any index, and the marriage register on film for your parish
begins in 1859. It would name both sets of parents.

===========================================================================
3. If it survives
===========================================================================

3a. A status animarum (stanje duša) for Otočac after 1846, or any household
list that shows ŠUMEĆICA No. 2. It would show who lived there and when
they were born, and whether the name Štrumbulko was kept beside Marić.

I am not asking blind about the books: the film shows the registers were kept
carefully, with the village and house number in the margin of each entry.

Whatever you can say, including that a book does not survive or is held
elsewhere, would help — and if the originals are held by the Državni arhiv u
Gospiću or by the diocese rather than the parish, I would be grateful to be told
where to write.

Thank you for your time, and for keeping these books.

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com
https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

I am researching the family of my grandmother, HEDVIGA "SEKA" BLAŽEVIĆ, born at
Senj in 1926. One of her ancestors on her mother's side (the PAPIĆ line) was CATHERINA
"CATTA" LUCKINIĆ of Karlobag. The work is published, free and without
advertising, at:

https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

Anything you send would be published there in full and credited. A negative
answer is worth having too, and I publish those as results.

WHAT I HAVE READ. Your death register records her on 29 May 1790 as
"Catharina annorum 70, vidua defti Jacobi Pilepich" — the widow of the captain
of the port. A family tree gives her birth as 30 March 1727, and her marriage to
Jacob Pilepich as 22 November 1747; I have found no document for the birth.

===========================================================================
1. Her baptism
===========================================================================

I read the baptismal book for 1691-1770 on the FamilySearch film (Hrvatski
državni arhiv). The year 1727 runs from image 49 to image 50. There is NO
Luckinić baptism on 30 March 1727 (the entry for that day is a daughter of Lovri
Bulanich), and none in May to August 1727 that I could read. The book's own
alphabetical index has no Luckinić at all.

1a. The baptism of CATHERINA LUCKINIĆ, most likely 1720-1730, with her
parents' names. If the filmed copy has missing leaves, or if her entry is
in another volume, I would be grateful to be told.

===========================================================================
2. A Luckinić household at Karlobag in 1727
===========================================================================

On 24 August 1727 the baptismal book names "the wife of Vicko Luckinich, called
Morica" as a godmother, so a Vicko Luckinić and his wife were living at Karlobag
that year. The FamilySearch index lists a Mare Luckinić baptised on 13 April 1725 to a
Vicko Luckinić; I have not seen that entry myself.

2a. The marriage of VICKO LUCKINIĆ and MORICA (Marija?), before 1725 — the
marriage register on film begins in 1736.
2b. The deaths of Vicko and Morica, which would give their ages.

===========================================================================
3. Where the originals are
===========================================================================

3a. Whether the registers of 1691-1770 are in the parish, or were transferred
to the Državni arhiv u Gospiću or the diocese — so that I write to the
right place.

Thank you for your time, and for keeping these books.

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com
https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

To: Ured Riječke nadbiskupije (address to confirm)
Subject: Upit o čuvanju matičnih knjiga — župa sv. Jakova Krmpote i Rijeka 1892

Poštovani,

obraćam Vam se na uputu vlč. Jakova Filipovića, župnika koji iz Ledenica
upravlja župom sv. Jakova Krmpote. Dana 15. rujna 2026. odgovorio mi je:

«Matice i arhiva svih župa kojim upravljam je predata u Riječku
Nadbiskupiju. Koliko mi je poznato oni su istu predali na skrb
Državnoga Arhiva. Budući mi ovdje na župama nemamo dodir sa starijim
Maticama, za daljnje informacije kontaktirajte Ured riječke
nadbiskupije.»

Ovo NIJE molba za istraživanje. Državni arhiv u Rijeci već mi je odgovorio da
ne obavlja istraživanja ove složenosti, i to u potpunosti razumijem i ne tražim
ponovno. Moje je pitanje drugačije i, nadam se, jednostavnije za Vas:

KOJE su knjige predane, i KOME?

Nadbiskupija je knjige predala i o toj primopredaji gotovo sigurno postoji
zapis. Taj zapis — popis, potvrda, primopredajni zapisnik — odgovorio bi na sve
niže navedeno odjednom, a nijedan arhivski djelatnik ne bi morao otvoriti
nijednu maticu.

Rado ću platiti naknadu. Ako Vam je lakše odgovoriti na hrvatskom, slobodno —
razumijem.

S poštovanjem,
David Defranceski

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

I am researching the family of my grandmother, HEDVIGA "SEKA" BLAŽEVIĆ, born at
Senj on 3 August 1926 and died at Johannesburg in 2001. The work is published,
free and without advertising, at:

https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

Anything you send would be published there in full and credited. A negative
answer is worth having too, and I publish those as results — the replies from
your Senj colleagues and from vlč. Filipović are already published as such.

WHY THIS IS A HOLDINGS QUESTION AND NOT A RESEARCH REQUEST
===========================================================================

One question is now asked from two directions and answered from neither.

* The PARISH says the registers went to the Archdiocese, and that the
Archdiocese passed them to the State Archive.
* The STATE ARCHIVE replied the same day that it does not undertake research
of this complexity. It did not say what it holds — which is fair, because
I had asked it to search rather than to list.

So nobody has yet said whether these books SURVIVE, or where they now are. The
Archdiocese is the one party that handed them over and would hold the transfer
record. That record is what I am asking for.

I have read the filmed copies (Hrvatski državni arhiv, through FamilySearch)
leaf by leaf. Every item below is something the films do NOT cover, and I say in
each case exactly where the film stops. I am not asking anyone to repeat work I
can do myself.

===========================================================================
1. SV. JAKOV KRMPOTE — sixty-four catalogued years that are not on the film
===========================================================================

The FamilySearch waypoint for Krmpote-Vodice is catalogued "Births 1815-1896".
THE FILM ITSELF BEGINS IN 1879: image 10 is page 2 and reads «Godine 1879». I
checked it leaf by leaf.

1a. Does a BAPTISMAL REGISTER for Sv. Jakov Krmpote covering the years
BEFORE 1879 survive, and who holds it now?

1b. Does any MARRIAGE REGISTER for that parish survive, of any period?
No marriage register for Sv. Jakov Krmpote is filmed at all — not a gap
in a range, the event type is simply absent.

What hangs on it: JURAJ «JURKO» BLAŽEVIĆ, a seljak of Smokvica Krmpotska house
114, is named in your register in 1895 — «Jurko Blažević i Tereza rođ.
Žubrinić, selj.», at the baptism of their son Marijan, 12 April 1895, page 168,
entry 26. His baptism, most likely 1855-1870, would name his father outright.
Five further generations, back to a Mateša Blažević born about 1750, rest on a
link no document yet states.

===========================================================================
2. RIJEKA, 1892 — a gap in the film, twice over
===========================================================================

LJUBOMIR «LJUBO» BLAŽEVIĆ was born at RIJEKA on 1 MARCH 1892. The filmed Rijeka
parish registers (koha:722509) run 1594-1920, and their own list of volumes
gives the baptisms as:

... Rodjeni 1880-1886 · 1886-1890 · 1890-1891 · 1900-1901 ...

There is no 1892-1899 baptismal volume on the film, and the alphabetical Kazalo
skips the same span — 1800-1889, then 1895-1902. The entry falls into a gap by
image and by index both.

2a. Does a RIJEKA BAPTISMAL REGISTER covering 1 MARCH 1892 survive, and in
whose care is it now?

A Krmpote peasant household had a child in Rijeka in 1892 and then went home —
the next child is baptised back at Krmpote in 1893. The entry would give the
address, and the address would explain why.

===========================================================================
3. THE TRANSFER RECORD ITSELF
===========================================================================

3a. If there is a PRIMOPREDAJNI ZAPISNIK or an inventory of what the
Archdiocese handed to the State Archive — for the Crikvenica deanery, or
for Sv. Jakov Krmpote specifically — a copy of that one document would
answer 1a, 1b and 2a together, and would tell me which volumes to ask
the State Archive for BY SHELFMARK rather than by description.

That last point is why I am writing to you rather than back to Rijeka. An
archive that will not search on a description will often produce a volume that
is named. I do not yet know the names.

Thank you for your time, and for keeping these books.

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com
https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

rows.what: Oskar Kosina's burial, Buenos Aires, 15 January 1954
rows.settles: The Zadar Franciscans ran the Croatian pastoral care in Argentina from 1929, so the 1954 funeral is in their custody's own papers and not in the later centre's books.
rows.draft:
DRAFT. 21 September 2026.
To: kustodijazadar@gmail.com
Franjevačka kustodija sv. Jeronima, Trg sv. Frane 1, 23000 Zadar
Kustos: fra Tomislav Šanko · tel 023/250-468
Subject: Upit — Oskar Kosina, umro u Buenos Airesu 15. siječnja 1954.

WHY ZADAR AND NOT BUENOS AIRES. The Croatian pastoral work in Argentina was
the Zadar Franciscans' from 1929, and fra LEONARD RUSKOVIĆ — the first Croatian
priest in Argentina — served from 1929 until his death in 1958, which means he
was the priest on the ground in January 1954. The Hrvatsko vjersko središte sv.
Nikole Tavelića did not yet exist in 1954, so the 1954 funeral is NOT in its
books; it is in whatever the custody's own people kept. And in JULY 2026 the
last Croatian friar, fra Josip Peranić, left Argentina after forty years, so
Buenos Aires now has no Croatian priest at all and Zadar is the address that
will still be there next year.

They have also just published a spomenica on the whole Argentine mission —
«Tejar – Buenos Aires: Hrvatsko vjersko središte 'Sv. Nikola Tavelić'» — so
somebody there has recently had the entire archive open on a desk.

The Buenos Aires centre itself: Av. dr. Ricardo Balbín 4925, 1430 Buenos Aires,
tel +54 11 4542 3400. NO EMAIL HAS BEEN VERIFIED for it. A city listing gives
`tehar@ciudad.com.ar`, which is an old ISP domain and unconfirmed — not written
to, because an unverified address is a stranger.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Poštovani oče kustose, poštovana braćo,

pišem Vam iz Australije. Vodim obiteljski arhiv obitelji Blažević i Kosina iz
Senja i molim Vas za pomoć oko jednoga našeg rođaka koji je umro u Argentini.

OSKAR KOSINA, rođen u Senju 1922., sin Pavla Kosine i Anke Blažević, umro je u
BUENOS AIRESU 15. SIJEČNJA 1954., u dobi od 31 godine. Znamo to iz njegove
tiskane sličice u spomen, koju obitelj još čuva.

Ovoga tjedna pronašli smo i njegov dolazak: u argentinskim lukama knjigama
upisan je kao

KOSINA, OSCAR — 25 godina — oženjen — «SEGKA» (Segna, tj. SENJ) — COLONO
Dolazak: 9. listopada 1947., parobrod PHILIPPA, ukrcaj u GENOVI

Dakle, izašao je preko Italije 1947. i umro šest godina kasnije.

Obraćam se upravo Vama jer je hrvatska pastva u Argentini od 1929. bila djelo
Vaše kustodije, a vlč. fra LEONARD RUSKOVIĆ, prvi hrvatski svećenik u
Argentini, ondje je djelovao od 1929. do svoje smrti 1958. — dakle i u
siječnju 1954. Hrvatsko vjersko središte sv. Nikole Tavelića tada još nije
postojalo, pa pretpostavljam da bi trag, ako ga ima, bio u zapisima Vaše braće,
a ne u knjigama Središta.

Molim Vas, ako je ikako moguće:

1. Postoji li u arhivu kustodije ikakav zapis o SPROVODU ili SMRTI Oskara
Kosine u siječnju 1954. u Buenos Airesu — knjiga umrlih, dnevnik, kronika
kuće, ili spomen u tadašnjem hrvatskom listu?
2. IME NJEGOVE SUPRUGE. To je ono što naša obitelj traži desetljećima.
U luku je stigao kao OŽENJEN, ali nijedna žena prezimena Kosina ne postoji
u argentinskoj bazi doseljenika — dakle vjenčao se u Europi, a ona je, ako
je došla, upisana pod djevojačkim prezimenom.
3. GDJE JE POKOPAN.
4. Znate li išta o njegovu sinu, rođenom u Argentini, koji je kasnije otišao u
Njemačku?
5. I jedno šire pitanje: u istom parobrodu PHILIPPA, šest mjeseci ranije
(1. travnja 1947.), stigao je i FRANJO KOSINA, 47 godina, agronom, upisan
kao «CROATA (HRVATSKA)». Sumnjamo da je bio brat našega pretka. Je li Vam
to ime poznato iz argentinske zajednice?

Znam da ste ovoga ljeta, odlaskom fra Josipa Peranića, zaključili četrdeset
godina njegova rada i, čini se, i samu hrvatsku franjevačku prisutnost u
Argentini. Upravo me to i potaknulo da pišem sada, dok je sjećanje i građa još
na okupu — čestitam Vam i na spomenici «Tejar – Buenos Aires».

Sve što naša obitelj ima o Oskaru i o njegovoj obitelji u Senju rado ću Vam
poslati, i javno je ovdje:

https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/kosina/

Hvala Vam od srca na svakom odgovoru, pa i na kratkom.

S poštovanjem,
David Defranceski
Arhiv obitelji Blažević
Australija

rows.what: A photograph of vlč. Anton Kosina (1921-2003) the family may publish, and what the mission holds of him
rows.settles: He founded the mission; its own papers are the best record of him, and the published press gives only 1958-1985.
rows.draft:
DRAFT — NOT SENT. 21 September 2026.
To: info@hkm-lu.de (Hrvatska katolička misija bl. Alojzija Stepinca,
Brandenburger Str., 67065 Ludwigshafen am Rhein)
Cc: —
Subject: Vlč. Anton Kosina (1921. – 2003.), utemeljitelj Vaše misije — obitelj iz Senja

WHY THIS LETTER. The mission he founded is the single best custodian of his
record: its own founding papers, a photograph, and almost certainly word of his
death in 2003. The published press gives 1958–1985 and nothing personal.

WHAT TO ASK FOR, in order of value:
1. A PHOTOGRAPH of vlč. Kosina that the family may publish, with a credit line.
2. His ORDINATION year and where.
3. Anything on his DEATH in 2003 — date, place, where he is buried.
4. Whether the mission holds anything of his: letters, parish bulletins, the
founding documents of 1967.
Offer in return: what this family holds — his birth parish, his parents, the
1943 raid that killed his father and two sisters, and his 1991 restoration of
his grandmother's grave in Senj. The mission will not have any of that.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Poštovani,

pišem Vam iz Australije, iz obitelji iz Senja. Vodim obiteljski arhiv
obitelji Blažević i Kosina iz Senja.

Utemeljitelj Vaše misije, vlč. ANTON (Ante) KOSINA, rođen u Senju
11. veljače 1921., umro 2003., bio je moj rođak — sin Pavla Kosine i Anke
Blažević. Njegov otac poginuo je u zračnom napadu na Senj 8. listopada 1943.,
a dvije sestre, Otilija i Neda, umrle su iste jeseni. Vlč. Kosina je 1991.
godine dao obnoviti grob svoje bake Tereze Žubrinić u Senju i potpisao se na
njemu: «OBNOVIO POP ANTE KOSINA ~ 1991».

Iz objavljenih izvora znamo da je 1958. došao iz Rima na područje
Kaiserslauterna kao svećenik tadašnje Riječko-senjske nadbiskupije, te da je
bio voditelj Vaše misije od njezina osnutka 1967. do 1985. godine. O
njegovu životu izvan toga ne znamo gotovo ništa.

Molim Vas, ako je moguće:

1. Posjedujete li FOTOGRAFIJU vlč. Kosine koju bismo smjeli objaviti na
obiteljskoj stranici, uz navođenje izvora?
2. Znate li godinu i mjesto njegova REĐENJA?
3. Imate li podatke o njegovoj SMRTI 2003. — datum, mjesto, gdje je pokopan?
4. Čuva li misija išta iz njegova vremena — dokumente o osnutku 1967.,
župne listove, pisma?

Rado ću Vam zauzvrat poslati sve što naša obitelj ima o njegovu podrijetlu i
obitelji u Senju — podatke iz matičnih knjiga, fotografije grobova i obiteljske
snimke — jer pretpostavljam da Vama to nije poznato.

Unaprijed najljepša hvala na svakom odgovoru.

S poštovanjem,
David Defranceski
[e-mail]
Arhiv obitelji Blažević — https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/kosina/

rows.what: The whole page of the landing book for the steamer PHILIPPA, 9 October 1947
rows.settles: Oskar Kosina landed married and no Kosina woman is in the free index under either spelling. The bound page lists everyone who sailed with him; it settles whether she is on it under a maiden name.
rows.draft:
DRAFT — NOT SENT. 21 September 2026.
To: base@cemla.com (Base de datos, CEMLA — Centro de Estudios Migratorios
Latinoamericano, Independencia 20, C1099AAN Buenos Aires)
Subject: Consulta — página del libro de desembarco, vapor PHILIPPA, 9 de octubre de 1947

WHY THIS LETTER. The free search gives one INDEX LINE per passenger and nothing
else. The bound entry books hold the whole page, and everyone who sailed with
him is on it. Oskar Kosina landed MARRIED on 9 October 1947 and NO Kosina woman
appears anywhere in the database under either spelling — so the woman this
archive is looking for is either on that page under a maiden name or she is not
in Argentina at all. The page settles it.

SECOND ASK, and cheaper for them: Franjo Kosina, same ship, 1 April 1947. If the
two men are connected, the two pages will show it — same sponsor, same
destination, consecutive entry numbers.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Estimados señores:

Escribo desde Australia. Mantengo el archivo histórico de una familia croata de
Senj, y su base de datos me ha permitido encontrar hoy el desembarco de un
pariente. Les agradezco muchísimo que este recurso exista y sea público.

El registro es el siguiente:

KOSINA, OSCAR — 25 años — C — YUGOSLAVA/S.H.S. — «SEGKA» — COLONO
Arribo: 9 de octubre de 1947 — vapor PHILIPPA — puerto de embarque: GÉNOVA

(«SEGKA» es Segna, el nombre italiano de la ciudad de SENJ, en Croacia. Oscar
Kosina nació allí en 1922 y falleció en Buenos Aires el 15 de enero de 1954.)

Quisiera consultarles:

1. ¿Es posible obtener una COPIA DE LA PÁGINA COMPLETA del libro de desembarco
correspondiente a ese arribo, o un certificado con todos los datos del
asiento? Me interesa especialmente saber si figuran el número de asiento, el
destino declarado y la persona o entidad que lo recibía.

2. El asiento indica que llegó CASADO. Sin embargo, no aparece ninguna mujer de
apellido KOSINA ni KOZINA en la base. ¿Podrían indicarme si en la misma
página, o en el mismo vapor, viaja alguna mujer que pudiera ser su esposa —
por ejemplo, con el mismo destino declarado o el mismo número de grupo
familiar? Ese dato es el que nuestra familia lleva décadas buscando.

3. En el mismo vapor PHILIPPA, seis meses antes, figura:
KOSINA, FRAJNO (Franjo) — 47 años — C — CROATA (HRVATSKA) — AGRÓNOMO
Arribo: 1 de abril de 1947 — PHILIPPA — GÉNOVA
¿Sería posible obtener también esa página? Sospechamos que era hermano de
nuestro antepasado y las dos fojas podrían confirmarlo o descartarlo.

Por supuesto abonaré el arancel que corresponda por la búsqueda y las copias.
Les ruego me indiquen el importe y la forma de pago.

Quedo muy agradecido por su tiempo.

Cordialmente,
David Defranceski

I am researching the family of my grandmother, HEDVIGA "SEKA" BLAŽEVIĆ, born at
Senj on 3 August 1926 and died at Johannesburg in 2001. The work is published,
free and without advertising, at:

https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

Everything you send would be published there in full, with your shelfmark, and
credited. I also publish my own errors — including, this month, the collapse of
my theory that an epidemic struck this family in 1845.

Three requests follow. Any one of them would be a real help; I do not expect all
three.


===========================================================================
1. BRINJE — the parish I have been ignoring for years
===========================================================================

This is the request I would choose if only one can be answered.

I have treated the KALANJ family as a Klenovica family throughout — I hold 216
Kalanj records, 119 of them at Klenovica. Their own baptismal entry says
otherwise, and I had read the line without acting on it. At the baptism of ANA
KALANJ, Klenovica house no. 22, 3 January 1864, the parents are entered as:

Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor,
BRINJENSIS PAROCHIAE RURICOLAE

— country people of the parish of BRINJE. My own records independently place
Rozalija Perković at Brinje, and hold a JURE BORIĆ of Brinje whose daughter Ana
(b. 12 February 1885, Brinje) married a PAPIĆ of Senj.

So three of my surnames — Kalanj, Perković and Borić — meet at Brinje, and I
have never opened a single page of that register.

1a. The MARRIAGE of JOSIP (Josephus) KALANJ, born 27 August 1826 at
Klenovica, to ROZALIJA PERKOVIĆ of Brinje — roughly 1840-1865. She died
25 September 1917. This entry would name her household, and it is the one
I want most.

1b. The BAPTISM of ROZALIJA PERKOVIĆ herself, roughly 1820-1835.

1c. Any decade of the Brinje registers, 1850-1890, in which KALANJ, PERKOVIĆ
and BORIĆ appear together — with HOUSE NUMBERS if the book gives them.
House numbers have done more for this research than names have.


===========================================================================
2. OTOČAC — the baptisms for PROZOR, 1875-1895
===========================================================================

I hold the household at PROZOR house no. 50 in detail: Michael Žubrinić, born
1826, and his seven children, Nikola 1858, Kata 1860, Georgius 1863, Magdalena
1865, Mate 1867, Ivan 1870, Franjo 1874.

And then my record stops. I have NOT ONE Žubrinić born at Prozor between 1875
and 1900.

American passenger manifests document exactly that missing generation leaving
Prozor, and name their fathers:

Eva Žubrinić b. 1880 sailed 1907 from Fiume
Nikola b. 1886 sailed 1911 father given as SANDRO Žubrinić
Anton b. 1891 sailed 1911 father given as MARCO Žubrinić
Miko b. 1893 sailed 1910 father given as IVAN Žubrinić
Mate b. 1867 sailed 1911 (this is the Mate born 1867 above)

Only one of those three fathers — Ivan — appears anywhere in my records. So
Prozor held at least two more Žubrinić households than I know of.

2a. The OTOČAC BAPTISMS covering PROZOR, 1875-1895. One volume, one village,
twenty years — and it would restore an entire generation at once.

2b. One entry I can give you an exact date for. A naturalisation petition
sworn at Brooklyn, New York, in 1939 gives IVAN ŽUBRINIĆ, BORN 30 JUNE
1888 AT OTOČAC. That is a sworn date, not a ship's estimate, so his
baptism should be in your register on that day. It would name his
parents. He is NOT the Ivan born 16 August 1887 at Otočac whom I already
hold.


===========================================================================
3. OTOČAC / ŠUMEĆICA — one man or two?
===========================================================================

My record gives one couple, MICHAËL ŽUBRINIĆ and MARIA née OREŠKOVIĆ, two sons
forty-six years apart:

Nicolaus, baptised 24 January 1834 — filius legitimus, Confiniarius ex Pago
Shumechicza No. 24, son of Michaël Xubrinich et Maria uxor ejus nata
Oreskovich

Nikola, born 23 August 1880 — named at his own marriage (Senj, 3 July 1910)
as son of the late Mate Žubrinić and Marija rodj. Orešković

Either one man married two women both called Maria, or — far likelier — there
were two men of the same name a generation apart and I have merged them.

3a. A MARRIAGE of a Michaël/Mate Žubrinić to a Maria Orešković at Otočac
BEFORE 1834, and a second such marriage roughly 1855-1870. If only one
exists, the merge is real but differently shaped.

3b. Any decade of the OTOČAC DEATH REGISTER between 1830 and 1860. I have
six people carrying the bare year "1845" with no day, month, place or
source, and I need to know when they actually died.

3c. If any STATUS ANIMARUM volume survives for Otočac or Šumećica, a
household page would answer more than any single entry — it lists a man,
his wife and his living children in one line of sight. I know these books
were kept in the region: a page of one from Our Lady of the Snow, Krivi
Put, running 1897-1939, survives in my own family papers.


Villages and house numbers already known to me, so any search can be narrow:
Šumećica 2 and 24 · Prozor 46, 50 and 245 · Dubrava 29 · Klenovica 22 and 23.

Thank you for your time.

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com
https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

I am researching the family of my grandmother, HEDVIGA "SEKA" BLAŽEVIĆ, born at
Senj on 3 August 1926 and died at Johannesburg in 2001. Her family were of this
parish for as far back as I can see: Papić, Blažević, Vukelić, Tomljanović,
Bezjak and Rogić — the surnames on the stones around their own.

The work is published, free and without advertising, at:

https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

Anything you send would be published there in full and credited.

The filmed copies of the Senj registers (Hrvatski državni arhiv, through
FamilySearch) stop at **1894 for baptisms** and **1907 for deaths**. I have read
those films — fifteen pages of the marriage book at full resolution, and the
whole of the year 1888 end to end. **Everything below falls after the films
stop**, which is why I am writing to the parish.

===========================================================================
1. Three deaths, and for the first one I can give you the page and the line
===========================================================================

1a. MILKA LUCIJA PAPIĆ (married Blažević), born Senj 9 October 1886,
died 1971.
Her baptismal entry — Senj births, str. 122, 1886 — carries an
annotation added by a registrar in **1971** citing her death entry at
**page 280, line 37**. Someone in this office closed that loop
eighty-five years later and left the reference behind. I would like the
entry it points to.

1b. ZVONIMIR MATEJ VUKELIĆ, born 13 January 1883, her first husband.
Married to her in this church on **4 November 1907** (Senj marriages,
p. 294, no. 30). He died in **1915**, leaving her a widow at twenty-eight
with a daughter of eight and a son of two. I know nothing else about him
— not the day, not the cause, not his trade.

1c. TEREZA BLAŽEVIĆ née ŽUBRINIĆ, born Otočac 29 November 1867, died at
Senj in **1931**. She was my great-great-grandmother.

===========================================================================
2. Two sisters recorded eighteen days apart, in January and February 1895
===========================================================================

The tree I inherited gives two daughters of the same Papić household born
**eighteen days apart** — which cannot be. Both fall in **January and February
1895**, and **the filmed baptismal register stops at 1894**, one year short.

2a. The BAPTISMS in the Senj register for JANUARY and FEBRUARY 1895 —
or simply a note of which of the two dates the register actually
carries.

===========================================================================
3. A question about this parish's own practice
===========================================================================

Reading the Senj baptisms and marriages I noticed something I cannot explain:
**Senj entries record no house number at all**, where the village books around
it — Krmpote, Krivi Put, Selce, Otočac — give one without hesitation.

3a. Does a STATUS ANIMARUM (stanje duša) survive for Senj? And were Senj
households numbered at all, the number simply not carried into the
registers?

I am not asking blind: I have just read the Karlobag status animarum right
through, and a page of a Krivi Put one, captioned "Our Lady of the Snow", runs
1897 to 1939 in my own family papers. So the books were kept in these parishes.

Thank you for your time, and for keeping these books.

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com
https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

I am researching the family of my grandmother, HEDVIGA "SEKA" BLAŽEVIĆ, born at
Senj on 3 August 1926 and died at Johannesburg in 2001. The work is published,
free and without advertising, at:

https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

Anything you send would be published there in full, with your shelfmark, and
credited. A negative result is worth having too, and I record those as results.

I have written separately to Gospić about the Otočac and Brinje parishes. The
three requests below are the ones that fall to Senj and Rijeka.


===========================================================================
1. SV. JAKOV KRMPOTE — the one link nothing states
===========================================================================

The Senj death register for 1907 (p. 225, entry 60) gives the birthplace of
TOMA BLAŽEVIĆ, nadničar, as the parish of SV. JAKOV KRMPOTE. That is the book
covering Smokvica Krmpotska, and it should hold every Blažević generation above
him.

Everything above JURAJ "JURKO" BLAŽEVIĆ — five further generations, back to a
Mateša Blažević born about 1750 — hangs on a link no document yet states. Juraj
is named as a parent by two separate Senj marriage registers (1919 and 1920) and
is placed at Smokvica house 114 in 1895. That is a strong circumstantial case. It
is not a sentence naming his father.

1a. The BAPTISM of JURAJ / JURKO BLAŽEVIĆ, Sv. Jakov Krmpote, most likely
1855-1870. This names his father outright.

1b. His MARRIAGE to TEREZA ŽUBRINIĆ (b. 29 November 1867, Otočac), most
likely 1885-1892, at Krmpote, Senj or Otočac. Names both fathers.

1c. His DEATH, Krmpote or Senj, before December 1920 — his son's marriage
entry of that month annotates him as dead.

What I already hold, so the search can be narrow: Juraj is a seljak, living at
SMOKVICA HOUSE 114 in 1895, entered there as "Jurko Blažević i Tereza rođ.
Žubrinić, selj." His children baptised in the parish are Ljubomir (b. Rijeka,
1 March 1892), Anka (1893), Marijan (b. 12 April 1895, entry 26, p. 168) and
Ruža (1897).

House 114 is a zadruga — three nuclear families of the descendants of Ilija
Blažević share the number across thirteen years: Toma Blažević and Terezija
Pećanić (1882, 1884), Pavao Blažević and Marija Tomljanović (1890), and Juraj
himself (1895).


===========================================================================
2. SENJ, 1915 — the death of ZVONIMIR VUKELIĆ
===========================================================================

ZVONIMIR MATEJ VUKELIĆ, born 13 January 1883, was the first husband of MILKA
LUCIJA PAPIĆ (b. Senj, 9 October 1886) — my great-grandmother. He died in 1915
and left her a widow at twenty-eight, with a daughter of eight and a son of two,
five years before she married Ljubomir Blažević on 8 December 1920.

I know nothing else about him at all.

2a. The SENJ DEATH REGISTER for 1915, for Zvonimir Vukelić — the date, the
cause, his occupation and his age.

Their MARRIAGE I already hold: Senj marriages p. 294, no. 30, 4 November 1907.
So the death falls between November 1907 and December 1920, and the family
account puts it in 1915. If 1915 yields nothing, that bracket is the range.


===========================================================================
3. A household that stood godparent twice and is in no tree
===========================================================================

Reading the godparent column of the Sv. Jakov Krmpote baptisms — a column I had
never read — turned up JANDRE BUTORAC and his wife MARIJA standing twice for
children of Toma Blažević at Smokvica house 114:

25 July 1882 Ivan Blažević — "Pere ?ećanić i Marija Butorac, supruga
Jandrina"
25 October 1884 Antonija "Tonka" Blažević — "Jandre i Marija Butorac,
supruzi, rimo-kat. seljaci"

Standing twice, two years apart, is a standing relationship between two
households — and Tonka is a direct ancestor of mine. Neither Jandre nor Marija
exists anywhere in my records.

3a. The MARRIAGE of a JANDRE (Andrija) BUTORAC at Sv. Jakov Krmpote, roughly
1870-1882 — with the HOUSE NUMBER of his household. If it sits near 114
the tie is neighbourhood; if it sits far off, it is much more likely kin.

3b. In the 1882 entry above, the godfather's surname is illegible in my copy —
it reads "Pere ?ećanić". If it is PEĆANIĆ he is the child's mother's own
kin. I would rather be told what the register says than guess.


===========================================================================
And one class of book, if any survives
===========================================================================

A STATUS ANIMARUM for Krivi Put, Sv. Jakov Krmpote, Smokvica Krmpotska or Senj
itself would answer more than several individual entries, because it lists a
household together.

I am not asking blind: a page of one survives in my own family papers, captioned
"Our Lady of the Snow, Krivi Put", running 1897 to 1939, with each person entered
as ž. (wife), s. (son), k. (daughter) or i. (child of) beneath the head of the
household. So the books were kept in these parishes.

For Senj there is a specific question attached. I have read Senj baptisms and
marriages and found that this town's entries record NO HOUSE NUMBER at all,
where the village books give one without hesitation. A Senj status animarum
would tell me whether the households were numbered and simply not carried into
the registers.

Thank you for your time.

David Defranceski
david.defranceski@gmail.com
https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

free and without advertising, at:

https://daviddef.github.io/TheBlazevic/

Anything you send would be published there in full, with your shelfmark, and
credited. A negative result is worth having too, and I record those as results —
your Senj colleague's reply is already published as one.

I have read the filmed registers (HDA copies, via FamilySearch) end to end where
they exist. Every request below is for something those films do NOT cover, and I
say in each case exactly where the film stops. I am not asking you to repeat work
I can do myself.

===========================================================================
1. RIJEKA, 1892 — a birth in your own city that I have never been able to place
===========================================================================

LJUBOMIR "LJUBO" BLAŽEVIĆ, my great-grandfather, was born on 1 MARCH 1892 at
RIJEKA. He married Milka Papić at Senj on 8 December 1920 (Senj marriages,
p. 366, entry 41) and died at Senj in 1966.

His parents were JURAJ "JURKO" BLAŽEVIĆ, a seljak of SMOKVICA KRMPOTSKA house
114, and TEREZA née ŽUBRINIĆ, born at Otočac on 29 November 1867. Their other
children were all baptised in the parish of Sv. Jakov Krmpote — Anka (1893),
Marijan (12 April 1895) and Ruža (1897).

1a. The BAPTISMAL ENTRY for Ljubomir Blažević, Rijeka, 1 March 1892 —
in whichever Rijeka parish it falls.

This is the one I would most like. **A Krmpote peasant household had a child in
Rijeka in 1892 and then went home** — the next child is baptised back at Krmpote
in 1893. The entry would give the address, and the address would explain why.

**Since drafting this I have found why I could not place it, and it narrows the
request considerably.** The filmed copy of the Rijeka parish registers (HDA,
through FamilySearch, catalogue koha:722509) runs from 1594 to 1920, and I have
now gone through its own list of volumes. The baptisms run:

... Rodjeni 1880-1886 · 1886-1890 · 1890-1891 · 1900-1901 ...

**There is no 1892-1899 baptismal volume on the film**, and the alphabetical
Kazalo skips the same span: it covers 1800-1889, then resumes at 1895-1902.
So Ljubomir's entry falls into a gap twice over, by image and by index.

**The volume itself must exist. It is simply not filmed** — which is exactly the
case where the archive can help and the film cannot. If you hold, or can say who
holds, the Rijeka baptismal register covering **1 March 1892**, that single entry
is the thing I have been unable to reach by any other route.

===========================================================================
2. SENJ — three deaths, all after the filmed register stops in 1907
===========================================================================

The Senj death register on film runs 1859-1907. All three of these fall after it.

2a. MILKA LUCIJA PAPIĆ, born Senj 9 October 1886, died 1971.
**I can give you the page and the line.** Her baptismal entry (Senj
births, str. 122, 1886) carries a registrar's annotation added in 1971
citing her death entry at **page 280, line 37**. A clerk closed that loop
eighty-five years later and left the reference behind.

2b. ZVONIMIR MATEJ VUKELIĆ, born 13 January 1883, Milka's first husband.
He died in 1915 and left her a widow at twenty-eight. Their marriage I
hold: Senj marriages p. 294, no. 30, 4 November 1907. So the death falls
between November 1907 and December 1920, and the family account says 1915.
I know nothing else about him at all — not the cause, not the day.

2c. TEREZA BLAŽEVIĆ née ŽUBRINIĆ, born Otočac 29 November 1867, died at
SENJ in 1931.

===========================================================================
3. SV. JAKOV KRMPOTE — where the film is sixty-four years short
===========================================================================

The FamilySearch waypoint for Krmpote-Vodice is catalogued "Births 1815-1896".
**The film itself begins in 1879**: image 10 is page 2 and reads Godine 1879.
I checked this leaf by leaf. Sixty-four catalogued years are not behind the
label, and they are the years I need.

3a. The BAPTISM of JURAJ / JURKO BLAŽEVIĆ, Sv. Jakov Krmpote, most likely
1855-1870 — before the film begins. This names his father outright.

Everything above Juraj — five further generations, back to a Mateša Blažević
born about 1750 — hangs on a link no document yet states. He is named as a
parent by two Senj marriage registers (1919, 1920) and placed at Smokvica house
114 in 1895. That is a strong circumstantial case. It is not a sentence naming
his father.

3b. His MARRIAGE to TEREZA ŽUBRINIĆ, before March 1892.
**The Krmpote waypoint has no marriage register at all**, and I have now
read the WHOLE of 1888 in the Senj marriage book — all thirty-nine
entries, 12 January to 15 November — and they are not in it.
**I have since also read the Rijeka marriage register to the end of the
filmed volume.** It is catalogued *Vjenčani 1866-1891*, and its last
entry is **9 August 1891**; I read every entry from April to that date,
about a hundred and twenty of them, and there is no Blažević and no
Žubrinić among them. So if they married at Rijeka it was after 9 August
1891 — in the same unfilmed span as their son's baptism. Otherwise the
marriage is at Krmpote, at Otočac, or somewhere I have not thought of.

3c. His DEATH, Krmpote or Senj, before December 1920 — his son's marriage
entry of that month annotates him as dead.

===========================================================================
4. A class of book, if any survives
===========================================================================

A STATUS ANIMARUM for SV. JAKOV KRMPOTE, KRIVI PUT, SMOKVICA KRMPOTSKA or SENJ
would answer more than several single entries, because it lists a household
together with dates of birth.

I am not asking blind. A page of one survives in my own family papers, captioned
"Our Lady of the Snow, Krivi Put", running 1897 to 1939. And I have just read the
Karlobag status animarum (HDA 715) right through, which shows what these books
give: a date of birth to the day for every soul in the house, and a communion
column for every year.

For SENJ there is a specific question attached. I have read Senj baptisms and
marriages and found that this town's entries record NO HOUSE NUMBER at all,
where the village books give one without hesitation. A Senj status animarum
would tell me whether the households were numbered and simply not carried into
the registers.

Thank you for your time.

David Defranceski
